en: The *Buddhavaṃsa*, Chapter 7: The *Revata-buddhavaṃsa*.
After Sumanas, there was...
The leader named Revata;
the peerless, incomparable,
matchless, supreme Victor.
He too, being entreated by Brahmā, proclaimed the Dhamma:
the analysis of the aggregates and the elements.
The non-occurrence of existence after existence.
Through his realization of this, three [knowledges] arose during his teaching of the Dhamma.
It cannot be reckoned by calculation;
it was the first realization [of the Truth] when [he saw] King Arindama.
The sage Revata entered parinibbāna;
at that time, there was a second realization of the truth by thousands of millions.
Having emerged from seven days of seclusion,
the Bull among Men [addressed] hundreds of millions of humans and devas.
When Revata, the great seer, attained the highest fruit, there were three assemblies.
Of those whose taints are destroyed, who are stainless,
well-liberated, and poised in equanimity—
beyond the path of calculation.
First were those who had assembled;
the second assembly consisted of one hundred thousand koṭis.
Even he who was peerless in wisdom and followed the Wheel—
he too was then afflicted by disease.
He had reached a state where his life was in peril. To him,
the Sages who then approached to inquire about his illness—
A third assembly occurred, consisting of a thousand koṭis of arahants;
at that time, I was there.
There was a brahmin named Atideva;
having approached the Buddha Revata,
I went to him for refuge.
Having praised his virtue, concentration,
and unsurpassed quality of wisdom according to my strength,
I gave him my upper robe.
That Buddha Revata, the leader of the world, also made a prediction concerning me.
“After immeasurable eons,
this one will become a Buddha.
Having exerted himself in striving...”
we shall face him directly.
Having heard those words of his as well,
I further clarified my mind;
I resolved upon higher vows for the fulfillment of the ten perfections.
Even then, having remembered that Buddha-dhamma, I cultivated it further;
I shall bring forth that Dhamma.
That which was my heart’s desire:
a city named Sudhaññavatī,
and a kshatriya named Vipula.
Vipulā was the mother of the great seer Revata;
she lived for six thousand years.
He dwelt in a house,
Sudassana, a jeweled throne adorned with a fillet.
Produced by meritorious deeds,
there are three supreme palaces and thirty-three thousand others.
The women were beautifully adorned;
the woman was named Sudassanā,
and her son was named Varuṇa.
Having seen four omens,
he went forth by means of a chariot;
for seven months less a few days, he remained.
The Conqueror, Revata, the Leader of the World, being entreated by Brahmā, applied himself to the supreme effort.
The Great Hero turned the wheel in the Varuṇa Grove at Sirīghara;
Varuṇa and Brahmadeva [were present].
They were his chief disciples;
the attendant of the great seer Revata was named Sambhava.
Bhaddā and Subhaddā were his chief female disciples;
he too was a Buddha, equal to the Unequaled.
At the foot of the Nāga tree you attained awakening.
Paduma and Kuñjara were the foremost attendants.
Sirīmā and Yasavatī were his chief attendants. In height, that Buddha—
Rising eighty cubits high,
it illuminates all directions like the risen banner of Indra.
An unsurpassed garland of radiance was produced from his body,
whether by day or by night.
It pervades a league all around.
For sixty thousand years,
such a lifespan exists.
Remaining for that long,
he brought many people across;
having displayed the power of a Buddha, he passed away.
Proclaiming the deathless in the world,
he, free from clinging, went out like a fire when its fuel is exhausted.
That body was like a jewel,
and that Dhamma was peerless;
all of that has vanished.
Indeed, all conditioned phenomena are empty.
Revata, Yasadharo, and the Buddha have attained Nibbāna in the Great City.
“The expansion of the [Buddha] element occurred in various regions.
This is the fifth lineage of the Blessed One Revata.
